4. Plaintiffs claimed that the properties in question belonged to Abdul Jalil and Abdul Gafur, two brothers, in equal shares, Plaintiffs are the sons and heirs of Abdul Gafur; plaintiff No. 1 also got the share of Abdul Mia, son of Abdul Jail, by gift. The other heirs of Abdul Jalil parted with their shares in favour of Abdur Rahman, predecessor of defendants 3 and 4. Defendants 3 and 4 having already withdrawn their share of the Compensation money, the plaintiffs are the only ones entitled to get the compensation under the award granted by the impugned Order in Misc. Case No. 6 of 1986-87. Plaintiffs' further case is that the recording of the Khatian in the name of Mahmuda Khatun along with her brothers Abdul Jalil and Abdul Gafur was wrong and that she had no title and interest in the suit land. 

 7. The learned Judges of the High Court Division upon examining the various provisions of the Ordinance observed that a special forum has been provided in the Ordinance for efficacious remedy against any award and "therefore, even without any further provision of express bar, it could he said that an action in the Civil Court against an award under the Ordinance is impliedly barred." Then reading Section 44 of the Ordinance which provides for express bar, it was further held that "it is clear that the suit in question is barred by law". As to the second relief relating to P. S. kahatian it was held that the plaintiffs have not sought for any consequential relief in respect of the alleged wrong recording of the khatian and, therefore, the suit cannot be maintained in respect of that prayer as well. With these findings, the plaint was rejected. 

 18. The learned Advocate for the appellants, at last, somewhat desperately tried to contend that the suit could not be barred altogether because there was another prayer (No.2) seeking declaration that the recording of the khatian in the a of Mahmuda Khatun was incorrect etc. The High Court Division found the said prayer to be of maintainable under Section 42 of the Specific Relief as no consequential relief was prayed for in respect of the alleged wrong recording of the khatian. It appears to us that prayer No. 1 was really the consequential relief which the appellants had prayed for in the suit. That prayer No. 1 being not maintainable, the other prayer cannot stand independently. Even otherwise the cause of action of the suit having been stated to be the order dated 22.9.86 passed in the Misc. Case No. 6/86-87 by defendants 12-14, the second prayer will be unsustainable for want of a cause of action, for, the stated cause of action will attract the bar of suit as already noticed. In any view of the matter the whole suit becomes barred under the law.
